# KPro v0.2.1

This pre-1.0 security patch hardens raw HTTP responses. Upgrade from v0.2.0.

## Security fix

When `httpx.Context.Write`, `Bytes`, `Stream`, or `CopyBody` wrote untrusted
bytes without an explicit response Content-Type, Go's automatic content
sniffing could classify HTML input as `text/html`. An application reflecting
that input could therefore expose reflected cross-site scripting.

Unspecified response types now default to `application/octet-stream`, and
Context responses set `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. Explicit application
Content-Type values and response bytes are preserved. Applications deliberately
serving HTML remain responsible for escaping untrusted input; direct native
ResponseWriter integrations retain their native responsibilities.

Tests use real HTTP connections to reproduce the HTML sniffing before the fix
and verify all four response methods after it. Go 1.26.9 remains the minimum.

## Compatibility

Applications relying on automatic response type detection must now select the
intended Content-Type explicitly. Text and JSON helpers already select theirs.
This intentional security behavior change does not alter KPro wire frames,
authentication boundaries, or the pre-1.0 API stability policy.
